newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UN trial rejects dismissal plea from Bosnian Serb.
newsitem.headline: UN trial rejects dismissal plea from Bosnian Serb.

text.p: The U.N. tribunal for the former Yugoslavia on Tuesday rejected a plea from Bosnian Serb defendant Dusan Tadic to have most of the war crimes charges against him dropped.

In a short statement, presiding Judge Gabrielle Kirk McDonald said the defence motion was denied and the trial would proceed as planned. Defence counsel lawyers had filed for dismissal of the bulk of the charges on August 20.
Tadic, a 40 year-old former cafe owner and police reservist, denies charges of killing, raping and toturing Moslems at Serb-run detention camps in northwest Bosnia in 1992.
The trial, which has heard from 75 prosecution witnesses since early May, resumes on Tuesday, having been delayed by Bosnia's first post-war elections at the weekend.

The only defence witness to testify so far, Robert McBeth Hayden, a professor of anthropology at the University of Pittsburg detailed the rising tide of nationalism in the former Yugoslavia which culminated in war.
Tadic is one of seven war crimes suspects in custody at the tribunal, which to date has indicted 75 suspects -- 54 Serbs, 18 Croats and three Moslems.
